content:
Outgoing Apple CEO Tim Cook's deliberately vague comments during an earnings call appear to suggest that heavy use of Siri AI could cost us more than we currently expect.

Although it has always been made clear that Siri AI cannot be used for free without limits, Cook's comments do seem to point to some bad news…

What we know

Apple's goal is to keep as much AI processing as possible on-device, which has a double benefit: on one hand it maximises user privacy protection, and on the other it means Apple doesn't have to pay AI server costs for those tasks. However, some tasks will still need to run on Apple's own Private Cloud Compute servers, and some will even need to call on Google Gemini servers.

Using these servers will of course generate costs for Apple, so it has always been clear that Apple would adopt the same freemium strategy for Siri AI as other companies apply to their chatbots: free use with a cap, with heavy users required to pay for a subscription.

However, until now the general assumption has been that all you need to use Siri AI is an iCloud+ subscription, and that the usage allowance may also be tied to the iCloud+ tier — that is, the 50GB plan comes with one allowance, the 200GB plan with a higher one, and the 2TB plan with more still.

This means that many of us could effectively get a higher Siri AI allowance through our existing iCloud+ plans.

But we may have to pay more

On the earnings call, Goldman Sachs put a related question to Cook.

His response seemed to go beyond simply pointing out the need for an iCloud+ subscription:

One reading is that heavy use of Siri AI would require not only an iCloud+ subscription but also an additional charge. In other words, the subscription wouldn't automatically bring us a higher usage allowance — it would merely give us the right to buy add-ons to increase the allowance.

His wording is ambiguous, so it doesn't necessarily mean this. However, if Cook had simply meant that higher usage allowances come bundled with an iCloud+ subscription, I would have expected him to say so more clearly. It is this vague wording that makes me suspect it may be bad news — or at least, taken at face value, the company hasn't decided yet but is considering the add-on approach.

Of course, none of this matters much until we know how our own Siri AI usage looks and when we might hit the cap. Even if my guess is right, it probably won't affect most Apple users. But looking at existing AI chatbots, most people who find them genuinely useful beyond occasional use end up having to buy a subscription.

What do you think? Do you share the same suspicions about what Cook's wording might be hinting at? And if so, do you think paying to use Siri AI would be worth it? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
